definition_zh: 乡村；农村地区；田园风光
definition_en: the land outside towns and cities, where fields and farms lie
core_image: 一条土路穿过麦田，尽头只有几座白墙农舍
scene: 车开出城市很远，窗外只剩麦田和几间农舍。The countryside began right after the last traffic light.
sceneCN: 这里 countryside 指「乡村地区」（第 1 个义项：城镇之外的田野与农舍）；句意是最后一个红绿灯过后，乡村就开始了。

pos.zh: 乡村；农村地区；田园风光

senses.title: Land beyond the town
senses.definition: the land outside towns and cities, where fields and farms lie
senses.definitionCN: 城镇之外、遍布田地与农场的地区
senses.example: We drove through the countryside for hours.
senses.exampleCN: 我们开车穿过乡村，走了好几个小时。
senses.why: A country has a side that was never paved over.
senses.whyCN: 一个国家总有一侧土地没被铺成马路。

senses.title: The rural scene
senses.definition: the natural scenery and slow life of rural areas
senses.definitionCN: 乡村地区自然的景色与缓慢的生活
senses.example: She loves the peace of the countryside.
senses.exampleCN: 她喜爱乡村的宁静。
senses.why: Fields and small houses paint a picture that cities cannot.
senses.whyCN: 田野和小屋画出城市画不出的图。

intro.en: Countryside joins country, from Latin contrata, land lying opposite, with side, the flank of a place.
intro.cn: countryside 由 country 与 side 合成；country 源自拉丁语 contrata（对面的那片地），side 意为事物的侧面。

items.en: Contrata meant the land lying over against the viewer.
items.cn: contrata 指横在观者对面的一片土地。

items.en: Contree named the land that lay around a town.
items.cn: contree 指环绕城镇展开的土地。

items.en: Country first meant a region or a nation.
items.cn: country 最初指一个地区或一个国家。

items.en: Countryside was coined to name the land beyond the town.
items.cn: countryside 被造出来，专指城镇之外的土地。

items.en: It now suggests fields, farms and a slower life.
items.cn: 今天它让人想到田野、农场和更慢的生活。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the country base, and the meaning group names other words for rural land.
note.cn: 形近组共享 country 这个词基，近义组列出其他表示乡野与景色的说法。

entries.definition: a nation or the land outside cities
entries.definitionCN: 国家，或城市之外的土地

entries.definition: a local government area
made to look rural
the visible shape of a stretch of land
the natural views of an area
a small group of houses in the country

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with the last street of a town, then move to fields and to a slow evening.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从城镇最后一条街开始，再到田野，最后到一个缓慢的傍晚。

normal.en: Country plus side: the side of a nation that stays green.
normal.cn: country 加 side：国家里保持绿色的那一侧。

normal.en: The city ends where the pavement stops and the soil begins.
normal.cn: 人行道结束、泥土开始的地方，城市就到头了。

normal.en: Fewer walls mean wider sky, and that is the countryside.
normal.cn: 墙更少，天更宽，这就是乡村。

normal.en: A farmhouse with one lamp is a whole map of the countryside.
normal.cn: 一间只点一盏灯的农舍，就是整幅乡村地图。

normal.en: If you hear birds instead of buses, you are in the countryside.
normal.cn: 听见鸟叫而不是公交车，你就在乡村了。

abstract.en: Picture a road that loses its white lines and turns to dust.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路失去白线，变成土路。

abstract.en: Picture a field that runs to the horizon without a fence.
abstract.cn: 想象一片田一直铺到天边，没有围栏。

abstract.en: Picture a night with more stars than street lamps.
abstract.cn: 想象一个星星比路灯多的夜晚。

examples.en: They moved to the countryside to grow vegetables.
examples.cn: 他们搬到乡下种菜。

examples.en: The countryside looks golden in late autumn.
examples.cn: 深秋时乡村一片金黄。

examples.en: A train crossed the quiet countryside at dawn.
examples.cn: 一列火车在黎明穿过安静的乡村。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 countryside 记成 country（国家）加 side（一边）：国家靠外的那一边，就是田野和农舍。

root: 由 country（乡野、国家）与 side（一侧）合成；country 源自拉丁语 contrata，本指横在城镇对面的那片地，即城镇之外的田野。

sensesIntro.en: From the land beyond the last street to the picture that land makes.
sensesIntro.cn: 从最后一条街之外的土地，到那片土地构成的图画。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a field path running past a few farmhouses.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条田间小路经过几座农舍。

branches.en: The land outside the town keeps its fields and farms.
branches.cn: 城镇之外的土地保留着田地与农场。

branches.en: That land also makes a picture people travel to see.
branches.cn: 那片土地还构成一幅人们专程去看的图。

branches.en: The same fields feed the farmer and please the visitor.
branches.cn: 同一片田养活了农人，也取悦了访客。

branches.en: Fewer buildings means a wider sky and a longer view.
branches.cn: 建筑更少，意味着天更宽、视野更远。

branches.en: Peace is the product of space and silence together.
branches.cn: 宁静是空间与寂静共同产生的。

intro.en: Countryside is a compound of country and side, two old English words joined into one place.
intro.cn: countryside 是 country 与 side 的复合词，两个古英语词拼成同一个地方。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base contrata, land lying opposite, still hides inside country.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 contrata（对面的土地）至今仍藏在 country 里。

items.example: The countryside is green in May.

items.meaning: a nation or its rural land
items.example: He left the country last year.
items.exampleCN: 他去年离开了这个国家。

items.example: A countryman showed us the path.
items.exampleCN: 一位乡下人给我们指了路。
那位农妇卖给我们鸡蛋。

items.example: The garden has a countrified look.
items.exampleCN: 这个花园有股乡野味道。

items.example: The house stands on this side.

items.meaning: the sloping side of a hill

items.example: We spent a week at the seaside.

definition_en: a local government area smaller than a state or province
core_image: 地图被细线切成许多方格，每格标着一个县名
scene: 地图上这一大片土地被分成许多小块，每块都写着一个县名。Our county has only one high school.
sceneCN: 这里 county 指「县」（第 1 个义项：州以下的行政区）；句意是我们县只有一所高中。

senses.title: A district of a state
senses.definition: a local government area in the United States, smaller than a state
senses.definitionCN: 美国州以下的行政区
senses.example: Our county builds and repairs the roads.
senses.exampleCN: 我们县负责修建和维修道路。
senses.why: A state is too large to know every farm, so it is cut into counties.
senses.whyCN: 一个州大到认不清每座农场，只好切成一个个县。

senses.title: A shire in Britain
senses.definition: a local government area in Britain, Ireland or Canada
senses.definitionCN: 英国、爱尔兰或加拿大的地方行政区
senses.example: Yorkshire is a large county in the north of England.
senses.exampleCN: 约克郡是英格兰北部一个大郡。
senses.why: Britain keeps the old lands that a lord once held.
senses.whyCN: 英国保留了旧时由领主掌管的那片土地。

senses.title: The people of a county
senses.definition: the people or the government of such an area, treated as one body
senses.definitionCN: 这样一个地区的居民或政府，被视为一个整体
senses.example: The county voted for a new library.
senses.exampleCN: 全县投票支持建一座新图书馆。
senses.why: Land and people share one name, so a county can speak with one voice.
senses.whyCN: 土地和人共用一个名字，所以一个县能用同一个声音说话。

intro.en: County comes from Latin comes, a companion, through Old French conte, a count, and comitatus, his land.
intro.cn: county 源自拉丁语 comes（同伴），经古法语 conte（伯爵）与拉丁语 comitatus（伯爵的领地）进入英语。

items.en: Comes meant a companion, often a man at court.
items.cn: comes 意为同伴，常指宫廷中随侍的人。

items.en: Comitatus named the land under a count.
items.cn: comitatus 指一位伯爵管辖的领地。

items.en: Conte named a count, a noble lord.
items.cn: conte 指伯爵，即一位贵族领主。

items.en: Counte first named the land a count ruled.
items.cn: counte 最初指伯爵所治理的土地。

items.en: It now names a local district in many countries.
items.cn: 今天它指许多国家里的地方行政区。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the count spelling, and the meaning group names other units of local land.
note.cn: 形近组共享 count 这个拼写，近义组列出其他表示地方行政区域的说法。

entries.definition: a nation or its rural land
to add up numbers in order
a record of money paid and owed
an area marked off for local government
entries.definitionCN: 为地方管理划出的一片区域

entries.definition: a large region under one government
entries.definitionCN: 归同一政府管辖的大区域

entries.definition: an old English county

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a count and his land, then move to a map of small squares.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一位伯爵和他的领地开始，再到一张切成小方格的地图。

normal.en: County hides the word count: the land a count once ruled.
normal.cn: county 里藏着 count：一位伯爵当年治理的地。

normal.en: A county is a slice of a state, thin enough to govern.
normal.cn: 县是州切下的一片，薄到足以治理。

normal.en: Every county on the map has a seat where the laws sit.
normal.cn: 地图上每个县都有一个安放法令的县城。

normal.en: The county fixes the roads you drive on every day.
normal.cn: 你每天开车经过的路，由县里来修。

normal.en: When the whole county votes, one voice carries far.
normal.cn: 全县投票时，一个声音能传得很远。

abstract.en: Picture a map ruled into squares by thin grey lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图被细灰线划成方格。

abstract.en: Picture a stone courthouse at the centre of those lines.
abstract.cn: 想象那些线中心的一座石造法院。

abstract.en: Picture a single road sign naming the county as you enter.
abstract.cn: 想象你驶入时那块写着县名的路牌。

examples.en: He works for the county as a road engineer.
examples.cn: 他在县里当道路工程师。

examples.en: The river marks the border between the two counties.
examples.cn: 这条河是两个县之间的界线。

examples.en: Our county is famous for its apples.
examples.cn: 我们县以苹果闻名。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 county 记成 count（伯爵）加 y：伯爵管的那片地，就是郡，再小一级就是县。

root: 源自拉丁语 comes（同伴、侍从），经古法语 conte（伯爵）与晚期拉丁语 comitatus（伯爵领地）进入英语，本指伯爵管辖之地，后成为县、郡一类行政区。

sensesIntro.en: From a count's land to a state district to the whole body of people living there.
sensesIntro.cn: 从伯爵的领地，到州以下的行政区，最后到住在其中的全体居民。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a map cut into squares, each with a name.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张被切成方格的地图，每格写着名字。

branches.en: A state is sliced into counties so each piece can be governed.
branches.cn: 州被切成一个个县，每片都能被治理。

branches.en: Britain keeps the older name for the same kind of land.
branches.cn: 英国用更古老的名字称呼同一种土地。

branches.en: The people inside the lines can vote and speak together.
branches.cn: 界内的居民能一起投票、一起发声。

branches.en: A county is both a piece of land and the body of people on it.
branches.cn: 县既是土地的一片，也是其上人群的整体。

branches.en: The old shire and its people still share one name.
branches.cn: 古老的郡与它的居民仍共用一个名字。

intro.en: County pairs the count base with the place ending -y, and grows a small family of compounds.
intro.cn: county 把 count 词基与表地点的词尾 -y 结合，又长出少量复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base comitatus, a count's land, still lies under the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 comitatus（伯爵领地）至今仍垫在这个词下面。

items.meaningCN: 归地方管理的一片区域
items.example: The county is small but busy.

items.exampleCN: 他们做了一次全县调查。

items.meaning: a person who lives in a county
items.example: Every countian knows the old bridge.
items.exampleCN: 每个县民都认得那座老桥。

items.meaning: a noble lord in old Europe
items.exampleCN: 那位伯爵拥有三个村庄。

items.example: They gave us a small discount.
items.exampleCN: 他们给了我们一点折扣。

definition_en: two people or things that go together, or to join two things
core_image: 两只手在桌子底下悄悄握在一起
scene: 雨里只有一把伞，两个人紧挨着走过马路。The couple shared one umbrella across the street.
sceneCN: 这里 couple 指「情侣」（第 2 个义项：成对相伴的两个人）；句意是那对情侣共撑一把伞过街。

senses.title: Two of a kind together
senses.definition: two people or things of the same kind that go together
senses.definitionCN: 同类的两个被放在一起的人或物
senses.example: I bought a couple of chairs for the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 我买了两把厨房用的椅子。
senses.why: Two things that belong together make one small team.
senses.whyCN: 两个彼此相属的东西，就组成一个小小的组合。

senses.title: Two people in love
senses.definition: two people who are married or in a romantic relationship
senses.definitionCN: 结了婚或处在恋爱关系中的两个人
senses.example: The couple moved in last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这对情侣去年春天搬了进来。
senses.why: Love turns two separate lives into one pair.
senses.whyCN: 爱情把两段各自的生活变成一双。

senses.title: To join two things
senses.definition: to join two things or ideas together
senses.definitionCN: 把两个事物或想法接在一起
senses.example: The engineer coupled the two pipes.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师把两根管子接了起来。
senses.why: Two ends meet and become one line.
senses.whyCN: 两个端点相接，就成了一条线。

intro.en: Couple comes from Latin copula, a bond, built from co-, together, and apere, to fasten.
intro.cn: couple 源自拉丁语 copula（纽带），由 co-（共同）与 apere（系上）构成。

items.en: Copula meant a band that ties two things.
items.cn: copula 意为把两样东西系住的带子。

items.en: Copulare meant to fasten things together.
items.cn: copulare 意为把东西系在一起。

items.en: Cople named a pair joined by a bond.
items.cn: cople 指被一条纽带系在一起的一对。

items.en: Couple first meant two things tied as one.
items.cn: couple 最初指被系成一体的两样东西。

items.en: It now names pairs of people as well as the act of joining.
items.cn: 今天它既指成对的人，也指连接这个动作。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the coup- shape, and the meaning group names other words for two things together.
note.cn: 形近组共享 coup- 这一词形，近义组列出其他表示「两个一起」的说法。

entries.definition: a device that joins two parts
entries.definitionCN: 把两个部件连起来的装置

entries.definition: two lines of poetry that rhyme
to hold someone close with care
two things of the same kind used together
two people who perform together
one of two people in a shared activity
entries.definitionCN: 共同活动中的两个人之一

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with one bond tying two things, then move to a pair in love and to pipes joined.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一根纽带系住两样东西开始，再到相爱的一对，最后到接起来的两根管子。

normal.en: A couple is two things held by one invisible band.
normal.cn: 一对就是被一条看不见的带子系住的两样东西。

normal.en: One umbrella and two shoulders: the picture of a couple.
normal.cn: 一把伞、两个肩膀，就是一对的样子。

normal.en: Say a couple of minutes and you mean two or three.
normal.cn: 说 a couple of minutes，意思就是两三分钟。

normal.en: To couple pipes is to let two ends kiss.
normal.cn: 把管子接起来，就是让两个端口相碰。

normal.en: A couple on a train ticket means one seat for two names.
normal.cn: 车票上的两个人，意味着两个名字共用一个座位。

abstract.en: Picture two rings linked through each other.
abstract.cn: 想象两枚戒指互相套住。

abstract.en: Picture two hands that refuse to let go.
abstract.cn: 想象两只不肯松开的手。

abstract.en: Picture one knot joining two short ropes.
abstract.cn: 想象一个结把两根短绳连成一根。

examples.en: A couple of students waited outside the office.
examples.cn: 两个学生在办公室外等着。

examples.en: The couple walked home along the river.
examples.cn: 这对情侣沿着河走回家。

examples.en: The wagon was coupled to the engine.
examples.cn: 车厢被挂到了火车头上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 couple 记成 copula（纽带）的同胞：一根带子把两个人系在一起，就是一对。

root: 源自拉丁语 copula（纽带、联结），由 co-（共同）与 apere（系上）构成，本指把两物系在一起之物，后指成对的人或物，也指连接这个动作。

sensesIntro.en: From two things tied by a bond, to two people in love, to the act of joining itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被纽带系住的两样东西，到相爱的一对，最后到连接这个动作本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one short band holding two objects.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条短带子把两个东西系在一起。

branches.en: Two things of a kind are tied into one small unit.
branches.cn: 同类的两个东西被系成一个小单位。

branches.en: Two people become a pair that others see as one.
branches.cn: 两个人成为别人眼中的一体。

branches.en: The verb keeps the old picture of a bond pulled tight.
branches.cn: 动词义保留了把纽带拉紧的旧画面。

branches.en: A pair is the result, coupling is the act.
branches.cn: 一对是结果，连接是动作。

branches.en: Love is a bond that people tie and keep.
branches.cn: 爱情就是人们自己系上并留住的纽带。

intro.en: Couple is a base word from Latin copula, extended by endings that mark pairs, joining and tools.
intro.cn: couple 是源自拉丁语 copula 的词根词，再由表示成对、连接与工具的各类词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: The bond base cop- still appears in copula and in the grammar term copular.
latinIntro.cn: 表示纽带的词基 cop- 仍出现在 copula 与语法术语 copular 中。

items.exampleCN: 三对伴侣共用一张桌子。

items.meaning: the act or part that joins
items.example: The coupling broke in the cold.

items.meaning: a device that joins two parts

items.example: The poem ends with a couplet.
items.exampleCN: 这首诗以一副对句结尾。

items.meaning: a linking word such as be
items.meaningCN: 像 be 这样的系动词
items.example: The copula links subject and noun.
items.exampleCN: 系动词连接主语与名词。

definition_en: a small printed piece of paper that gives a discount or can be exchanged for something
core_image: 一张从报纸上剪下的小纸片，边上留着虚线齿孔
scene: 结账时她从钱包里抽出一张剪下来的小纸片，抵掉了两块零钱。She handed the cashier a coupon for the soap.
sceneCN: 这里 coupon 指「优惠券」（第 1 个义项：结账时抵扣钱款的小纸片）；句意是她把一张肥皂优惠券递给收银员。

senses.title: A ticket that cuts the price
senses.definition: a printed ticket that takes money off what you buy
senses.definitionCN: 买东西时能减掉一部分钱的印刷票据
senses.example: She saved five dollars with a coupon.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一张优惠券省了五块钱。
senses.why: A small promise of a lower price, printed on paper.
senses.whyCN: 把「价格更低」这个承诺印在一张小纸上。

senses.title: A paper exchanged for a gift
senses.definition: a printed piece of paper that can be exchanged for a service or a gift
senses.definitionCN: 可用来换取某项服务或赠品的印刷纸片
senses.example: The coupon entitles you to one free drink.
senses.exampleCN: 这张券让你免费得到一杯饮料。
senses.why: Paper stands in for the thing you will receive.
senses.whyCN: 纸片先替你将要点到的东西站在这里。

senses.title: An interest slip on a bond
senses.definition: a detachable part of a bond that is clipped off to claim interest
senses.definitionCN: 债券上可剪下来领取利息的附券
senses.example: He clipped the coupon and collected the interest.
senses.exampleCN: 他剪下息票，领走了利息。
senses.why: Every payment once had its own small paper to cut.
senses.whyCN: 从前每一笔利息都有一张小纸片等着被剪下。

intro.en: Coupon comes from French couper, to cut, itself from Latin colpus, a stroke or blow.
intro.cn: coupon 源自法语 couper（切），其更早的来源是拉丁语 colpus（击打）。

items.en: Colpus meant a stroke or a blow.
items.cn: colpus 意为一次击打。

items.en: Couper meant to cut something off.
items.cn: couper 意为把某物切下来。

items.en: Coupon named a piece cut from a larger sheet.
items.cn: coupon 指从大张纸上切下的一小片。

items.en: English coupon first named an interest slip cut from a bond.
items.cn: 英语 coupon 最初指从债券上剪下的息票。

items.en: It now usually means a ticket that cuts the price.
items.cn: 今天它通常指能减价的票据。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the coup- shape, and the meaning group names other papers of value.
note.cn: 形近组共享 coup- 这一词形，近义组列出其他有价票据的说法。

entries.definition: a sudden and clever success
a car with two doors and a low roof
a throat illness of young children
a paper that can be used as money
a small object or card that stands for value
entries.definitionCN: 代表某种价值的小物件或卡片

entries.definition: a printed card that lets you enter or travel
entries.definitionCN: 允许入场或乘车的印刷卡片

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a slip cut from a sheet, then move to a free drink and to bond interest.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从大纸上剪下的小片开始，再到一杯免费饮料，最后到债券利息。

normal.en: Coupon begins with coup, a cut: it is a piece cut from a sheet.
normal.cn: coupon 开头是 coup（切）：它是从大张纸上切下的一片。

normal.en: The dotted line is there so your fingers know where to cut.
normal.cn: 虚线印在那里，是为了让手指知道该从哪儿剪。

normal.en: A coupon is a price cut carried in your pocket.
normal.cn: 优惠券就是装在口袋里的降价。

normal.en: Older bonds paid you by slips you clipped at the edge.
normal.cn: 旧时债券靠你从边上剪下的票券付息。

normal.en: If the paper can be exchanged, it is a coupon.
normal.cn: 只要这张纸能换东西，它就是券。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of scissors resting beside a newspaper page.
abstract.cn: 想象一把剪刀搁在报纸页旁边。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pushing a small slip across the counter.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把一张小票推过柜台。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag with a corner torn away.
abstract.cn: 想象一张价格标签被撕掉一角。

examples.en: This coupon is valid until the end of June.
examples.cn: 这张优惠券有效期到六月底。

examples.en: He collected coupons from the newspaper every Sunday.
examples.cn: 他每个星期天都从报纸上剪优惠券。

examples.en: You can redeem the coupon at any branch.
examples.cn: 你可以在任何一家分店兑换这张券。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 coupon 记成 coup（切）加 on：从大张纸上切下来的一小片，就是能换东西的券。

root: 源自法语 couper（切），再往前是拉丁语 colpus（击打）；coupon 本指从大张纸上剪下的一小片纸，后指可剪下兑取的息票与优惠券。

sensesIntro.en: From a slip cut off a bond, to a paper that lowers a price, to a paper that buys a gift.
sensesIntro.cn: 从债券上剪下的票，到能降价的纸片，最后到能换赠品的纸片。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small slip cut from a larger printed sheet.
core.cn: 核心意象：从大张印刷纸上剪下的一小片。

branches.en: The slip carries a promise of paying less.
branches.cn: 这张小片带着少付一点钱的承诺。

branches.en: The same slip can stand for a drink or a gift.
branches.cn: 同样的小片也能代表一杯饮料或一份赠品。

branches.en: On old bonds the slip was cut to claim interest.
branches.cn: 在旧债券上，剪下这张小片就能领息。

branches.en: Both are paper that buys something without money.
branches.cn: 两者都是不用钱就买到东西的纸。

branches.en: A coupon is always a claim waiting to be clipped.
branches.cn: 优惠券永远是一张等着被剪下的索取凭据。

intro.en: Coupon is built on the French cutting base coup-, extended by the noun ending -on.
intro.cn: coupon 建立在法语表示切的词基 coup- 上，再加名词词尾 -on。

latinIntro.en: The cutting base goes back to Latin colpus, a blow, which also shapes coup and recoup.
latinIntro.cn: 表示切的词基可追到拉丁语 colpus（一击），coup 与 recoup 也由它构成。

items.meaning: a slip cut from a sheet

items.example: She keeps coupons in a box.
items.exampleCN: 她把优惠券收在盒子里。

items.example: A keen couponer never pays full price.
items.exampleCN: 爱用券的人从不付全价。

items.example: The coupon book has ten pages.

items.meaning: a set of letters typed for a discount
items.meaningCN: 网上结账时输入的折扣代码
items.example: Enter the coupon code at checkout.
The deal was a coup for the team.
items.exampleCN: 这笔交易对团队来说是一次漂亮的胜利。

items.example: They recouped their costs in a year.
items.exampleCN: 他们一年内收回了成本。

definition_en: the ability to face danger or pain without letting fear stop you
core_image: 一个人腿在发抖，还是向前迈出了一步
scene: 火警响起，他还是冲进屋里抱出了孩子。It took courage to run into the burning house.
sceneCN: 这里 courage 指「勇气」（第 1 个义项：面对危险仍向前的能力）；句意是冲进着火的房子需要勇气。

senses.title: Strength before danger
senses.definition: the ability to face danger or pain without letting fear stop you
senses.definitionCN: 面对危险或痛苦时不被恐惧挡住的力量
senses.example: It took courage to enter the dark cave.
senses.exampleCN: 走进那个黑漆漆的山洞需要勇气。
senses.why: Fear shouts stop, and courage takes one more step.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧喊着停下，勇气却再迈一步。

senses.title: Strength to do what is hard
senses.definition: the strength to do something difficult or unpopular
senses.definitionCN: 去做困难或不受欢迎之事的力量
senses.example: She had the courage to say no.
senses.exampleCN: 她有胆量说不。
senses.why: Saying no to a crowd needs a voice of your own.
senses.whyCN: 对着一群人说「不」，需要有自己的声音。

senses.title: A steady inner confidence
senses.definition: a feeling of confidence that lets a person try
senses.definitionCN: 让人敢于尝试的一种内在信心
senses.example: The good news gave him courage.
senses.exampleCN: 这个好消息给了他底气。
senses.why: A little proof can turn doubt into a steady breath.
senses.whyCN: 一点点证明，就能把疑虑变成平稳的呼吸。

intro.en: Courage goes back to Latin cor, the heart, through Old French corage, the heart as the seat of brave feeling.
intro.cn: courage 可追溯到拉丁语 cor（心），经古法语 corage（作为勇敢之情所在的心）进入英语。

items.en: Cor meant the heart and the feelings seated there.
items.cn: cor 意为心，以及安放在心里的情感。

items.en: Coraticum named the feelings that rise from the heart.
items.cn: coraticum 指从心里升起的情绪。

items.en: Corage meant the heart as the source of brave feeling.
items.cn: corage 指作为勇敢之情来源的心。

items.en: Courage first meant the heart and its moods.
items.cn: courage 最初指心以及心的各种状态。

items.en: It now names the strength to meet danger.
items.cn: 今天它专指迎接危险的那股力量。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same courage base, and the meaning group names other words for boldness.
note.cn: 形近组收集建立在 courage 词基上的词，近义组列出其他表示勇敢的说法。

entries.definition: to give someone hope and support
to take away someone's confidence
showing no fear when there is danger
the quality of facing danger without fear
entries.definitionCN: 面对危险不畏惧的品质

entries.definition: the cool boldness to do a hard thing
the willingness to take a risk

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a beating heart, then move to a voice that says no and to a steady breath.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一颗跳动的心开始，再到一个敢说「不」的声音，最后到平稳的呼吸。

normal.en: Courage holds the Latin word for heart, cor.
normal.cn: courage 里藏着拉丁语的心，cor。

normal.en: Fear is loud, but courage is the step you take anyway.
normal.cn: 恐惧很响，勇气是你照样迈出的那一步。

normal.en: A person of courage feels fear first and moves after.
normal.cn: 有勇气的人先感到害怕，然后才动。

normal.en: Moral courage is saying no when everyone nods.
normal.cn: 道德勇气就是众人都点头时你说不。

normal.en: One kind word can hand someone else your courage.
normal.cn: 一句好话就能把你的勇气递到别人手里。

abstract.en: Picture a small flame that refuses to go out in wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一小簇在风里也不肯熄灭的火。

abstract.en: Picture a foot lifted while the whole body shakes.
abstract.cn: 想象全身发抖时仍抬起的一只脚。

abstract.en: Picture a door opened onto a dark room.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门朝黑屋子被推开。

examples.en: It takes courage to admit a mistake.
examples.cn: 承认错误需要勇气。

examples.en: She found the courage to speak in front of the class.
examples.cn: 她鼓起勇气在全班面前发言。

examples.en: His courage during the flood saved two families.
examples.cn: 他在洪水中的勇气救了两家人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 courage 记成 cor（心）加 age：心里憋着的那股劲儿，就是勇气。

root: 源自拉丁语 cor（心），经古法语 corage 进入英语，本指心以及心的情感，后专指面对危险时从心里生出的力量。

sensesIntro.en: From the heart in danger, to the voice that refuses, to the quiet confidence that remains.
sensesIntro.cn: 从危险中的那颗心，到敢于拒绝的声音，最后到留下的那份安静的底气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shaking leg taking one firm step forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：发抖的腿向前迈出坚定的一步。

branches.en: The body wants to run and the heart decides to stay.
branches.cn: 身体想逃，心却决定留下。

branches.en: Doing the hard right thing needs a voice of your own.
branches.cn: 去做艰难而正确的事，需要有自己的声音。

branches.en: Confidence grows when someone believes in you.
branches.cn: 有人相信你时，底气就长出来。

branches.en: Both danger and disapproval test the same heart.
branches.cn: 危险与反对考验的是同一颗心。

branches.en: A steady heart can both refuse and begin.
branches.cn: 一颗稳的心既能拒绝，也能开始。

intro.en: Courage is built on the heart base cour-, which grows verbs with en- and dis- and adjectives with -ous.
intro.cn: courage 建立在表示心的词基 cour- 上，再由 en- 与 dis- 造动词，用 -ous 造形容词。

latinIntro.en: The heart base cor still beats inside courage, cordial and record.
latinIntro.cn: 表示心的词基 cor 仍跳动在 courage、cordial 与 record 里。

items.example: A courageous driver stopped the bus.
items.exampleCN: 一位勇敢的司机把车停住了。
她的鼓励让我坚持下去。

definition_en: a series of lessons, the way something develops, or one part of a meal
core_image: 一条跑道从脚下一直伸到看不见的远处
scene: 新生拿着课表在教学楼里找自己那门课。She signed up for a course in Italian cooking.
sceneCN: 这里 course 指「课程」（第 1 个义项：一系列有安排的课）；句意是她报名了一门意大利烹饪课。

senses.title: A set of lessons
senses.definition: a series of lessons on one subject
senses.definitionCN: 围绕一个科目安排的一系列课
senses.example: She is taking a course in French.
senses.exampleCN: 她正在修一门法语课。
senses.why: Learning is a road with a set number of steps.
senses.whyCN: 学习就是一条设有固定步数的路。

senses.title: The way time runs
senses.definition: the way something develops over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 事物在一段时间里发展的方式
senses.example: In the course of the year the town changed.
senses.exampleCN: 在这一年里，这座小镇变了。
senses.why: Time runs like water and marks its own channel.
senses.whyCN: 时间像水一样奔流，并留下自己的河道。

senses.title: One part of a meal
senses.definition: one of the parts of a meal, served separately
senses.definitionCN: 一餐中单独上桌的其中一道
senses.example: The main course was fish.
senses.exampleCN: 主菜是鱼。
senses.why: A meal is served in stages, like a road in stretches.
senses.whyCN: 一顿饭分段上桌，就像一条路分成几段。

intro.en: Course comes from Latin cursus, a running or a race, from currere, to run.
intro.cn: course 源自拉丁语 cursus（奔跑、赛跑），来自动词 currere（跑）。

items.en: Cursus meant a running or a race.
items.cn: cursus 意为奔跑或赛跑。

items.en: Currere meant to run quickly.
items.cn: currere 意为快速奔跑。

items.en: Cours named the path a river or a race follows.
items.cn: cours 指河流或赛跑所循的路线。

items.en: Course first meant the way something runs.
items.cn: course 最初指事物奔行的方式。

items.en: It now covers lessons, meals and the passage of time.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖课程、菜式与时间的流逝。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words that sound like course, and the meaning group names other words for a path or a lesson.
note.cn: 形近组收集与 course 读音相近的短词，近义组列出其他表示路线与课程的说法。

entries.definition: rough in texture
a wish that harm will come to someone
the reason why something happens
a period of teaching one subject
entries.definitionCN: 教授某个科目的一节课

entries.definition: the way from one place to another
entries.definitionCN: 从一地到另一地的走法

entries.definition: a series of changes that lead to a result
entries.definitionCN: 通向结果的一系列变化

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a running track, then move to time flowing and to a dish carried in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一条跑道开始，再到流动的时间，最后到端上桌的一道菜。

normal.en: Course comes from a word for running, so every course is a track.
normal.cn: course 来自表示奔跑的词，所以每一门课都是一条跑道。

normal.en: A course of study has a start, a middle and a finish line.
normal.cn: 一门课程有起点、中间和终点线。

normal.en: In the course of a day, the sun draws the same arc.
normal.cn: 一天的过程里，太阳画出同一道弧。

normal.en: The main course arrives when the road of dinner is halfway.
normal.cn: 主菜上来时，晚餐这条路正好走到一半。

normal.en: Of course means the road is clear: no doubt at all.
normal.cn: of course 表示路很清楚：毫无疑问。

abstract.en: Picture a river cutting its own channel through soil.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河在泥土里切出自己的河道。

abstract.en: Picture footprints in a straight line across a field.
abstract.cn: 想象田野上一串笔直的脚印。

abstract.en: Picture plates arriving one after another on a table.
abstract.cn: 想象盘子一个接一个端上桌。

examples.en: The course lasts twelve weeks.
examples.cn: 这门课持续十二周。

examples.en: In the course of the meeting she said nothing.
examples.cn: 会议进行过程中她一言未发。

examples.en: We had soup, then a fish course.
examples.cn: 我们喝了汤，然后上了一道鱼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 course 记成 cur（跑）加 se：一条被人跑出来的路，既是路线，也是要走完的课程。

root: 源自拉丁语 cursus（奔跑、跑道），来自动词 currere（跑），经古法语 cours 进入英语，本指跑出的路线，后引申为过程、课程与一餐中的一道菜。

sensesIntro.en: From a track that is run, to the flow of time, to one stage of a meal.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被跑过的跑道，到时间的流动，最后到一餐中的一个阶段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a track running from the feet to the horizon.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条从脚下伸向天边的跑道。

branches.en: A course of lessons is a track with numbered steps.
branches.cn: 一门课程就是标好步数的跑道。

branches.en: Time runs forward and leaves a channel behind.
branches.cn: 时间向前奔流，留下一条河道。

branches.en: A meal moves in stages, each one a short stretch.
branches.cn: 一餐分阶段推进，每一段都不长。

branches.en: Both a lesson plan and a life have a course to finish.
branches.cn: 课程表与人生都有一条要走完的路。

branches.en: From the flow of time to the order of dishes, sequence rules.
branches.cn: 从时间的流动到菜的顺序，都是先后在起作用。

intro.en: Course is built on the Latin running base curs-, which also gives current, courier and excursion.
intro.cn: course 建立在拉丁语表示奔跑的词基 curs- 上，current、courier 与 excursion 也由它构成。

latinIntro.en: The running base curr- still runs through current, courier and occur.
latinIntro.cn: 表示奔跑的词基 curr- 至今仍贯穿 current、courier 与 occur。

items.example: The course is open to all.
Blood was coursing through his veins.
Coursework counts for half the mark.

items.meaning: a book used in a course
items.example: Open your coursebook to page ten.
The current pulled the boat away.

items.meaning: a person who runs with messages
items.exampleCN: 一名快递员送来了包裹。

definition_en: a place where legal cases are judged, an area for a ball game, or the home of a king
core_image: 高背木椅后挂着国徽，椅子下方站着两排人
scene: 法官敲下小锤，庭下所有人立刻安静下来。The whole court waited for the judge to speak.
sceneCN: 这里 court 指「法院」（第 1 个义项：审理案件的场所）；句意是整个法庭都在等法官开口。

senses.title: The room of law
senses.definition: a place where legal cases are heard and judged
senses.definitionCN: 审理并判决法律案件的场所
senses.example: The case will come to court next month.
senses.exampleCN: 这个案子下个月开庭。
senses.why: When two sides cannot agree, they bring the quarrel to one room.
senses.whyCN: 当两边谈不拢，就把争执搬进同一间屋子。

senses.title: The ground for a game
senses.definition: an area marked out for a ball game
senses.definitionCN: 为球类运动划出的场地
senses.example: They booked a tennis court for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 他们订了一小时网球场。
senses.why: A game needs lines before it can have rules.
senses.whyCN: 比赛先要有线，才谈得上规则。

senses.title: The house of a king
senses.definition: the home and household of a king or queen
senses.definitionCN: 国王或女王的居所与随从群体
senses.example: The young prince grew up at court.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻的王子在宫廷里长大。
senses.why: Power always gathers around one seat.
senses.whyCN: 权力总要聚到同一把椅子周围。

intro.en: Court comes from Latin cohors, an enclosed yard and the guard around a leader, through Old French cort.
intro.cn: court 源自拉丁语 cohors（围起的院子、首领身边的卫队），经古法语 cort 进入英语。

items.en: Cohors meant an enclosed yard or a band of soldiers.
items.cn: cohors 意为围起的院子或一队士兵。

items.en: The word named both the yard and the guard around a leader.
items.cn: 这个词同时指院子和围绕首领的卫队。

items.en: Cort named the yard of a castle and the lord's household.
items.cn: cort 指城堡的院子和领主的家眷随从。

items.en: Court first meant the yard where a lord lived.
items.cn: court 最初指领主居住的院落。

items.en: It now names law courts, ball courts and royal households.
items.cn: 今天它指法院、球场与王室宫廷。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words close in sound, and the meaning group names places of judgement, enclosure and rule.
note.cn: 形近组收集读音接近的短词，近义组列出与审判、围合和统治有关的场所。

entries.definition: a unit of liquid equal to two pints
entries.definitionCN: 等于两品脱的液体单位

entries.definition: short in a way that seems rude
a piece of clothing worn over other clothes
entries.definitionCN: 穿在其他衣服外面的外套

entries.definition: a body that judges special cases
an enclosed area beside a building
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物旁边的围起空地

entries.definition: the large official home of a ruler
entries.definitionCN: 统治者居住的宏大官邸

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a yard behind a wall, then move to a judge and to a game on marked ground.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从墙后的一处院子开始，再到一位法官，最后到划好线的比赛场地。

normal.en: A court was first a yard: four walls around some ground.
normal.cn: court 最初就是院子：四面墙围住一块地。

normal.en: The same walls now hold a judge instead of a lord.
normal.cn: 同样的墙里如今坐着法官，而不是领主。

normal.en: A tennis court is just an empty yard with white lines.
normal.cn: 网球场不过是一个画了白线的空院子。

normal.en: To court someone is to stand in their yard and hope.
normal.cn: 追求一个人，就是站在人家院外满心期待。

normal.en: At court, everyone watches the one chair.
normal.cn: 在宫廷里，所有人都盯着那把椅子。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden hammer coming down on a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一把木锤落在桌面上。

abstract.en: Picture white lines painted on red ground.
abstract.cn: 想象红地上画出的白线。

abstract.en: Picture a row of tall chairs facing one taller chair.

examples.en: They play basketball on the court behind the school.

examples.en: The queen held court in the great hall.

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 court 记成「考他」：把人带上法庭考问一番，院子就成了审案的地方。

root: 源自拉丁语 cohors（围起的院子、首领的卫队），经古法语 cort 进入英语，本指领主的院落与随从，后指宫廷、法庭与球场。

sensesIntro.en: From an enclosed yard to the room of law, the marked ground of a game and the seat of a king.
sensesIntro.cn: 从围起的院子，到审案的屋子、划线的球场，最后到国王的居所。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: four walls closing around a piece of open ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：四面墙围住一块空地。

branches.en: The enclosed yard becomes the room where law is spoken.
branches.cn: 围起的院子变成宣读法律的那间屋子。

branches.en: The same enclosed ground is marked out for a game.
branches.cn: 同样的围合空地被划线用来比赛。

branches.en: A ruler keeps a court of guards, clerks and suppliants.
branches.cn: 统治者身边聚着卫兵、文书与求见者。

branches.en: Both are bounded spaces where rules decide what counts.

intro.en: Court is a base word from Latin cohors, extended by endings and by compounds with room, house and yard.

latinIntro.en: The Latin yard base cohort- also appears in cohort, a group of soldiers.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示院子的词基 cohort- 也出现在 cohort（一队士兵）里。

definition_en: an open space surrounded by the walls of a building or buildings
core_image: 四面房子围出一块方地，中间种着一棵小树
scene: 推开木门，四面都是房，中间那块空地种着一棵小树。Children ran around the courtyard after dinner.
sceneCN: 这里 courtyard 指「庭院」（第 1 个义项：被房屋四面围住的空地）；句意是晚饭后孩子们在庭院里跑来跑去。

senses.title: A yard inside the walls
senses.definition: an open area surrounded by the walls of a building
senses.definitionCN: 被建筑物墙体围住的空地
senses.example: The old house has a stone courtyard.

senses.why: Four walls turn a piece of sky into a private room.

senses.title: The air well of a big building
senses.definition: a narrow open space inside a large building that lets in light and air

senses.example: The museum is built around a quiet courtyard.

senses.why: Buildings need a hole to breathe through.
senses.whyCN: 房子需要一个洞，才能呼吸。

intro.en: Courtyard joins court, from Latin cohors, an enclosed yard, with yard, from Old English geard, a fenced ground.
intro.cn: courtyard 由 court（源自拉丁语 cohors，围起的院子）与 yard（源自古英语 geard，围起的地）合成。

items.en: Cohors meant an enclosed yard or a guard.
items.cn: cohors 意为围起的院子或卫队。

items.en: Geard meant a fenced piece of ground.
items.cn: geard 意为用篱笆围起的一块地。

items.en: Court named the yard of a castle.
items.cn: court 指城堡里的院子。

items.en: Courtyard joined court and yard into one word.
items.cn: courtyard 把 court 与 yard 合成一个词。

items.en: It now names any open space closed in by walls.
items.cn: 今天它指任何被墙围合的空地。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the two halves of the compound and one court word, and the meaning group names other enclosed open spaces.

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with four walls around a tree, then move to light falling into a narrow well.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从围住一棵树的四面墙开始，再到光线落进狭窄的天井。

normal.en: Court plus yard: a yard that a court of walls holds.
normal.cn: court 加 yard：被一圈院墙捧住的院子。

normal.en: The sky above a courtyard is a square of blue.
normal.cn: 庭院上方的天空是一块方形的蓝。

normal.en: One tree in the middle is enough to make it a garden.
normal.cn: 中间种一棵树，它就够得上一个花园。

normal.en: Rain falls into a courtyard and stays for a while.
normal.cn: 雨落进庭院，会多停一会儿。

normal.en: A courtyard keeps the street outside and the family inside.
normal.cn: 庭院把街道留在外面，把家人留在里面。

abstract.en: Picture a square of sky framed by four roofs.
abstract.cn: 想象四个屋顶框出的一方天空。

abstract.en: Picture footsteps echoing on stone after rain.
abstract.cn: 想象雨后石地上回荡的脚步声。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden gate opening onto still air.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇木门推开一片静止的空气。

examples.en: A well stands in the middle of the courtyard.
examples.cn: 庭院中间有一口井。

examples.en: The students crossed the courtyard to reach the library.
examples.cn: 学生们穿过庭院去图书馆。

examples.en: Ivy covered the courtyard wall.
examples.cn: 常春藤爬满了院墙。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 courtyard 记成 court（院落）加 yard（场地）：两个院子叠在一起，就是四面围住的庭院。

root: 由 court（院落、宫廷）与 yard（围起的场地）合成；court 源自拉丁语 cohors（围起的院子），yard 源自古英语 geard（围起来的地）。

sensesIntro.en: From a private square of ground to the narrow well that lets a big building breathe.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一块私人的方形地面，到让大楼得以呼吸的狭长天井。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: four walls holding a square of ground and sky.
core.cn: 核心意象：四面墙围住一方土地与天空。

branches.en: The walls turn open ground into a private room without a roof.
branches.cn: 墙把空地变成一间没有屋顶的私人房间。

branches.en: Deep inside a big building, the well lets light fall through.
branches.cn: 在大楼深处，天井让光线落下来。

branches.en: Both are holes left in a building on purpose.
branches.cn: 两者都是建筑里故意留下的空洞。

branches.en: A tree and a well make the yard a small living world.
branches.cn: 一棵树和一口井，让院子成为一个小世界。

branches.en: Air moves up through the well and cools the rooms.
branches.cn: 空气沿天井上升，让四周的房间凉下来。

intro.en: Courtyard is a compound of court and yard, and both halves still work alone.

latinIntro.en: The court half keeps the Latin base cohors, an enclosed yard.
latinIntro.cn: court 这一半保留着拉丁词基 cohors，意为围起的院子。

definition_en: a child of your uncle or aunt, or a distant relative
core_image: 过年时一屋子小孩被大人按辈分排成一排
scene: 过年时她被妈妈推到一个陌生男孩面前，说这是你表哥。She met her cousin for the first time at the family dinner.
sceneCN: 这里 cousin 指「表兄弟姐妹」（第 1 个义项：姑舅姨的孩子）；句意是她在家庭聚餐上第一次见到表兄。

pos.zh: 堂兄弟姐妹；表兄弟姐妹；远亲

senses.title: A child of your uncle
senses.definition: the child of your uncle or aunt
senses.definitionCN: 你叔叔、舅舅、姑母或姨母的孩子
senses.example: My cousin lives in the next town.
senses.exampleCN: 我表哥住在邻镇。
senses.why: Two families branch out from the same trunk.
senses.whyCN: 两个家庭从同一根树干上分出来。

senses.title: A relative far up the tree
senses.definition: any relative who is not close but shares an ancestor
senses.definitionCN: 关系不近、但共有一位祖先的亲戚
senses.example: He is a distant cousin of the painter.
senses.exampleCN: 他是那位画家的远房亲戚。
senses.why: The family tree keeps branching long after the names fade.
senses.whyCN: 名字都记不清了，家谱还在继续分叉。

intro.en: Cousin comes from Latin consobrinus, the child of a mother's sister, through Old French cosin.
intro.cn: cousin 源自拉丁语 consobrinus（姨母的孩子），经古法语 cosin 进入英语。

items.en: Consobrinus named the child of a mother's sister.
items.cn: consobrinus 指母亲姐妹的孩子。

items.en: Com- together and sobrinus cousin built the word.
items.cn: com-（共同）与 sobrinus（表亲）合成了这个词。

items.en: Cosin widened the sense to any uncle's child.
items.cn: cosin 把意思扩大到任何叔伯姑舅姨的孩子。

items.en: Cousin entered English with that wider sense.
items.cn: cousin 带着这个更宽的意思进入英语。

items.en: It now also covers relatives far out on the family tree.
items.cn: 今天它还包括家谱上关系很远的亲戚。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words close in sound to cousin, and the meaning group names other family words.
note.cn: 形近组收集与 cousin 读音接近的词，近义组列出其他亲属称谓。

entries.definition: to trick someone for money
a soft pad to sit or rest on
a function used in trigonometry
entries.definitionCN: 三角学中使用的一种函数

entries.definition: a person connected to you by family
a male relative of your blood
entries.definitionCN: 有血缘关系的男性亲属

entries.definition: the son of your brother or sister

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with children of two brothers, then move to a tree that keeps branching.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从两兄弟的孩子开始，再到一棵不断分叉的家谱树。

normal.en: Two brothers start two families, and their children are cousins.
normal.cn: 两兄弟开两支家，他们的孩子就是表亲。

normal.en: A cousin is a brother with a different address.
normal.cn: 表兄弟就是住在另一个地址的兄弟。

normal.en: At the family dinner, cousin is the name for the child you do not know yet.
normal.cn: 在家宴上，cousin 就是你还没认熟的那个孩子。

normal.en: Climb high enough on the tree and everyone becomes a cousin.
normal.cn: 在家谱上爬得够高，人人都成了亲戚。

normal.en: A distant cousin shares a great grandparent and little else.
normal.cn: 远房亲戚只共一位曾祖，别的几乎不共。

abstract.en: Picture two branches leaving one thick trunk.
abstract.cn: 想象两根枝条从同一根粗树干分出去。

abstract.en: Picture two children pushed together by grown hands.
abstract.cn: 想象两个小孩被大人的手推到一起。

abstract.en: Picture a family tree fading at its far edges.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵家谱树在远端渐渐模糊。

examples.en: My cousin taught me to swim.
examples.cn: 我表哥教会了我游泳。

examples.en: All my cousins came to the wedding.
examples.cn: 我的表亲们都来参加了婚礼。

examples.en: She is a cousin on my father's side.
examples.cn: 她是我父亲那边的表亲。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cousin 记成 co（共同）加 sin（同一血脉）：共着一份血脉的人，就是堂表亲。

root: 源自拉丁语 consobrinus（姨母的孩子），由 com-（共同）与 sobrinus（表亲）构成，经古法语 cosin 进入英语，泛指叔伯姑舅姨的孩子，也指远亲。

sensesIntro.en: From the child of an uncle or aunt to any relative far out on the family tree.
sensesIntro.cn: 从叔伯姑舅姨的孩子，到家谱上关系很远的所有亲戚。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two branches leaving the same family trunk.
core.cn: 核心意象：两根枝条从同一根家谱树干分出。

branches.en: The children of two siblings are cousins to each other.
branches.cn: 两个兄弟姐妹的孩子彼此是堂表亲。

branches.en: Far up the tree, the shared ancestor is the only link.
branches.cn: 在家谱高处，共有的祖先成了唯一联系。

branches.en: Both senses rest on one ancestor and two family lines.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在一位祖先与两条家系上。

branches.en: The near cousin is met at dinners and holidays.
branches.cn: 近亲常在饭桌和节日上见面。

branches.en: The far cousin may be known only from a story.
branches.cn: 远房亲戚也许只从故事里听说过。

intro.en: Cousin is a French borrowing whose family is built with the endings -ly and -hood.
intro.cn: cousin 是来自法语的借词，它的词族靠 -ly 与 -hood 等词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base consobrinus, a mother's sister's child, lies under the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 consobrinus（姨母的孩子）垫在这个词下面。

a cousin one generation further out

items.meaning: an old phrase for a first cousin
items.example: The will named a cousin german.
items.exampleCN: 遗嘱里提到一位嫡亲表亲。

definition_en: to put something over another thing, to include, or the front of a book
core_image: 一块布被抖开，盖住桌上的所有东西
scene: 天要下雨，她抓起一块塑料布把整堆柴火盖住。She used a cloth to cover the bread on the table.
sceneCN: 这里 cover 指「覆盖」（第 1 个义项：把东西盖在上面）；句意是她用一块布盖住了桌上的面包。

senses.title: To lay something over
senses.definition: to put something over a thing so that it is hidden or protected
senses.definitionCN: 把东西盖在另一物上，使它被遮住或受保护
senses.example: She covered the bread with a cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一块布盖住了面包。
senses.why: A cover is a second skin laid over the first.
senses.whyCN: 覆盖物就是披在原来那层皮上的第二层皮。

senses.title: To include a whole range
senses.definition: to include a subject, an area or a cost
senses.definitionCN: 把某个主题、区域或费用包含在内
senses.example: The book covers the whole history of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书涵盖了这座城市全部的历史。
senses.why: A wide cloth thrown over many objects holds them all.
senses.whyCN: 一块大布盖在许多东西上，就把它们全兜住了。

senses.title: The front of a book
senses.definition: the outer front part of a book or a magazine
senses.definitionCN: 书或杂志最外面的正面部分
senses.example: The cover shows a blue mountain.
senses.exampleCN: 封面画的是一座蓝色的山。
senses.why: The first thing you see is the cloth over the contents.
senses.whyCN: 你最先看到的，是盖在内容外面的那块布。

intro.en: Cover comes from Latin cooperire, to hide completely, built from co-, wholly, and operire, to shut.
intro.cn: cover 源自拉丁语 cooperire（完全遮住），由 co-（全然）与 operire（关上）构成。

items.en: Operire meant to shut or to hide something.
items.cn: operire 意为关上或遮住某物。

items.en: Cooperire meant to hide a thing all over.
items.cn: cooperire 意为把一物整个盖住。

items.en: Covrir meant to put something over a thing.
items.cn: covrir 意为把东西盖在上面。

items.en: Cover first meant to protect something with a layer.
items.cn: cover 最初指用一层东西保护某物。

items.en: It now also means to report, to include and to pay for.
items.cn: 今天它也表示报道、涵盖与支付。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words near cover in shape, and the meaning group names other ways of hiding or shielding.
note.cn: 形近组收集与 cover 形状接近的短词，近义组列出其他遮蔽与保护的说法。

to want what another person has
a small green plant with three leaves

to fold paper or cloth around a thing
